licensing._note: Read by js/main/license-store.js (LicenseStore.policy). alphaClosesAt null = the alpha is open: every install is free, the Settings > License card offers the free-for-good alpha claim, and the updater gates nothing. Set it (YYYY-MM-DD) on the same day LICENSE_ALPHA_CLOSES_AT is set on Connect; after that date unlicensed installs get trialDays of updates, then the updater stops offering newer builds (the app itself never locks). price is copy only, and null (since 2026-09-02) means NO number is quoted anywhere: the Settings card then says the price is not set yet.

llamacppInstall._sha256Note: Pins MUST match the URLs above. When bumping the llama.cpp build (bNNNNN), recompute: curl -sL <url> | shasum -a 256. A mismatch aborts the install (SECURITY-AUDIT.md M4). Bumping here is also how existing installs upgrade: when this pin is ahead of the on-disk build, Settings > AI Assistant > Your Models shows an Update engine row.

embeddingModel._note: The Library's local semantic index (docs/LIBRARY.md). name+storeDims are the index identity: changing either makes every install wipe and rebuild its derived index (originals untouched). The prefixes are EmbeddingGemma's mandatory asymmetric task templates; they must change with the model. Keep the fallback copy in main.js embeddingModelSource() in the same commit.

models.name: anjadhe-qwen3.5:4b
models.desc: Anjadhe's own model: Qwen3.5 4B tuned for email insights and the assistant's tools — light and fast on 8-16 GB Macs

_minRamNote: Small-machine tiers are served by anjadhe-qwen3.5:4b since 2026-08-29 — Anjadhe's own tune of Qwen3.5-4B (HF anjadhe/anjadhe-qwen3.5-4b; docs/SMALL_MODEL.md has the full gate evidence). It is the recommended default for 8-16 GB Macs; the interim stock qwen3.5:9b/4b entries (2026-08-26) are out of the catalog — the 9B had to go because the wizard recommends the highest minRam tier that fits, which would outrank the tuned model on 16 GB Macs. Installs keep anything already downloaded. The low-RAM step still offers Anjadhe Cloud below 8 GB.
_releasedNote: Each model's `released` is the provider's publication date of the base model (Hugging Face base instruct repo createdAt) — NOT the GGUF quant repo's lastModified, which gets bumped by README edits. Shown in Settings as 'Released <Mon YYYY>'. Refresh when reviewing the catalog each release (RELEASING.md step 2a).
_ggufSha256Note: Set each model's gguf.sha256 to pin it (SECURITY-AUDIT.md M4): curl -sL <url> | shasum -a 256. Empty string = unverified (download proceeds with a console warning until pinned).
_visionNote: A gguf.mmproj sidecar marks a local model as vision-capable: it is downloaded next to the weights and passed to llama-server via --mmproj, and its presence is what the app's image-attachment gating keys on. mmproj URLs/hashes get the same review-and-pin treatment as gguf.sha256 (RELEASING.md step 2a). visionModels lists model-name prefixes (case-insensitive) that accept image input on the BYOK cloud engines; custom 'Your server' entries are assumed capable (the server rejects images it can't handle).
_taskGradeNote: taskGrade: true marks a model certified for task mode (multi-step plan execution) — the evidence bar is the full agent-evals scorecard (det + model journeys) PLUS a clean live fan-out run (docs/TASK_ENGINE.md). Task mode suggests a task-grade brain when the active one isn't; it never switches silently. Cloud engines and custom servers are assumed task-grade. Review per release with the model catalog (RELEASING.md step 3a).
_feedPostsNote: Posts published into every user's home feed (PromptFeed). Fields: id (stable string — dismissals key on it), title, date (ISO), body (markdown), optional link {url, label}. Dismissed ids are stored per-user in the synced 'dismissed-feed-posts' key.

feedPosts.title: Welcome to your feed
feedPosts.body:
This is your home stream. Ask the assistant anything in the box above, and let **routines** fill this space on their own.

A routine is an instruction Anjadhe runs for you — on a schedule (a morning briefing at 8, a reflection every Sunday) or when something happens (an email arrives, a file lands in a folder). Each run posts its result here.

A few come ready-made — Daily Briefing, Morning News, Weekly Reflection — so posts will start landing without you doing anything. To adjust them or add your own, open **Manage routines** above, or just tell the assistant what you want: "every weekday at 5pm, summarize what I got done today."

Anjadhe occasionally shares product news in this space too; dismiss any post with the corner button.

feedPosts.title: A model made for small Macs
feedPosts.body:
Anjadhe now has its own local model: **anjadhe-qwen3.5:4b**, a fine-tune of Qwen3.5 4B built specifically for the work this app does all day — reading email into insights, managing tasks and goals, answering questions about your own data. It is light enough to run well on 8 and 16 GB Macs, and it was trained entirely on synthetic data: no user data, ever.

On smaller Macs, setup now recommends it automatically. Already set up? Find it under **Settings › AI Assistant › + Add model › On this Mac**. The model card and weights are public on Hugging Face.
